Author: Itinerant18
Message:
feat: add Sentry to all three apps with shared PII scrubbing

Phase 2 of the hardening plan. Sentry was entirely absent — no @sentry/*
dependency, no config, no instrumentation — so the only observability was Vercel
Speed Insights.

@sentry/nextjs v10 on Next 14.2.4 (its declared peer range is ^13.2 || ^14 ||
^15 || ^16, checked rather than assumed). Per app: client/server/edge configs,
instrumentation.ts, and a global-error boundary.

Scrubbing is the point of this change, so it lives in ONE place —
packages/utils/src/sentry-scrub.ts — rather than three copies that would drift
invisibly. sendDefaultPii: false stops the SDK volunteering IPs and cookies, but
says nothing about what this app itself puts into events, so scrubSentryEvent
also:

  - drops request cookies, bodies and query strings outright (booking ids,
    postcodes and signed-URL tokens all travel in the query string)
  - reduces `user` to an id — no email, username or IP
  - redacts sensitive keys at depth in extra/contexts/tags/breadcrumbs:
    addresses, phone numbers, postcodes, lat/lng, full names, UTRs, OTPs,
    booking start codes, tokens and secrets
  - regex-redacts JWTs, Stripe keys, PaymentIntent client secrets, webhook
    secrets and UK phone numbers out of free-text messages, where a structured
    field never sees them

Session Replay is deliberately NOT enabled: it records the DOM, which on these
apps means addresses and KYC documents, and beforeSend cannot reach inside a
replay recording.

Two integration points that would have made this monitoring-that-isn't:

  - tunnelRoute: '/monitoring' routes browser events through our own origin so
    ad blockers cannot drop them. But the provider and admin middleware gate
    everything except /login, so the tunnel would have been redirected and
    client errors would silently never arrive. All three matchers now exclude
    it. Verified at runtime: on the provider app `/` returns 307 to /login while
    /monitoring does not redirect.
  - The four existing error boundaries accepted `error` and ignored it. A
    boundary swallows the error, so that whole class of client render failures
    was invisible. They now captureException.

Everything is DSN-gated: with no DSN, init() is skipped entirely, so local
development and any un-provisioned environment behave exactly as before. Source
map upload likewise no-ops without SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN rather than failing the
build.

Verified beyond the build passing, because a green build does not exercise any of
this:

  - apps/*/.next/server/instrumentation.js is emitted in all three, which Next
    only does when experimental.instrumentationHook is actually honoured — that
    flag is load-bearing for ALL server and edge capture on Next 14, and nothing
    else would have caught it being ignored.
  - Zero *.js.map under apps/*/.next/static, so widenClientFileUpload has not
    started shipping client source. deleteSourcemapsAfterUpload only runs after
    an upload, which does not happen without an auth token, so this needed
    checking rather than assuming.
  - The /monitoring tunnel rewrite is present in routes-manifest.json and the
    compiled middleware regexp excludes it.

sentrySampleRate() instead of Number(process.env.X ?? 0.1): an env var that
exists but is blank — trivial to create in a Vercel dashboard — coerces to 0
under Number() and silently disables tracing. Same silent-no-op shape as the
Upstash shim.

Tests: 32 files / 219 passing, 0 skipped. sentry-scrub.test.ts covers the
scrubbing including a cyclic object and multi-secret strings;
sentry-wiring.test.ts guards the triplicated config against drift (every runtime
must import the shared scrubber, set sendDefaultPii: false, stay DSN-gated, and
never enable Replay; middleware must not gate the tunnel).

To switch on: set NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN and/or SENTRY_DSN per Vercel project.
SENTRY_ORG/PROJECT/AUTH_TOKEN additionally enable readable stack traces. All
documented in .env.example.

Note for the Cloudflare phase: /monitoring is a new unauthenticated POST and is
not under /api/*, so a WAF or bot rule that only exempts /api/* will block it
silently. Recorded in the plan file.

Author: Itinerant18
Message:
fix(bookings): fail fast on card bookings without Stripe, no ghost bookings on payment failure

QA's 'cash booking hits Stripe error' was actually the card path: the form
defaults to 'Pay now', and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY= (empty string) slipped past the
'?? placeholder' fallback, sending an empty Bearer header. A direct repro
confirmed the cash path never touches Stripe.

- integrations/stripe: treat empty/whitespace key as missing (new
  stripeConfigured()); '' no longer reaches the Stripe client
- createBooking: card + no Stripe key now throws a clear error BEFORE any
  insert; previously it created the booking, dispatched provider offers, and
  then died at intent creation, leaving pending_match ghosts with live offers
- createBooking: offers dispatch only after the payment path is established,
  and a payment-setup failure now cancels the booking row
- book flow: when the server has no Stripe key the 'Pay now' option is
  disabled with an explanation and cash becomes the default

Description: Uncovered a JSON Web Token, which may lead to unauthorized access to web applications and sensitive user data.
Author: Itinerant18
Message:
fix(matching): filter training-ineligible providers in findCandidates

The cascade offered gated-category jobs to providers who could not accept them:
gating was enforced only at the accept boundary (training_required throw) and in
the SQL admin engine, not in findCandidates. Every such offer burned its TTL, and
because recompute_acceptance counts both declined and expired against
acceptance_rate (0003_triggers), providers took a hit to 20% of their matching
score for jobs they were never eligible to take. A gated category with no trained
providers spent OFFER_TTL x cascade depth — about 30 minutes — of dead offers per
booking before reaching unmatched.

findCandidates now drops ineligible candidates after the availability filter and
before the cap, reusing the tested isCategoryTrainingEligible core. The
observation metric moves with the decision: one offer.blocked_training event per
skipped provider, stage 'candidate_filter', so the observation window still
measures demand held back by training gates — without creating offers nobody can
act on. The accept-path check stays as defence in depth for offers that predate
an eligibility change, now reporting stage 'accept'; the payload type documents
that rows without a stage predate the filter.

training-filter.db.test.ts proves both directions against the local stack, with
fixtures it creates and removes itself: an untrained provider is excluded and the
filter-time event is written; upserting a passing completion puts them back in
the candidate list. The first version of the fixture scheduled the booking at
now+24h — outside the provider's seeded working hours — and the availability
filter dropped them before training was consulted, which is exactly the ordering
the test now pins: the booking is placed inside a seeded availability slot so the
training filter is the only thing under test. Self-skips when the local stack is
down, same as the RLS suite.

90 tests, typecheck clean, all three apps build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Uncovered a JSON Web Token, which may lead to unauthorized access to web applications and sensitive user data.
Author: Itinerant18
Message:
feat(dev): local Supabase stack, seed data, and RLS/grant tests

Development ran against the production project. Every `pnpm dev` session read and
wrote live data, there was no reset, and logging in locally cost a real Twilio SMS
because test_otp only applies to a local stack.

- supabase/seed.sql: 2 providers (one approved+online, one pending KYC), 2
  customers with real lat/lng addresses, provider_services, availability slots and
  time off, bookings across assigned/on_the_way/in_progress/completed/cancelled, a
  live pending offer, reviews, payments and payouts. Seeds auth.users and lets the
  existing handle_new_user trigger create profiles, rather than duplicating that.
- apps/*/.env.local.example: local API URL and the standard Supabase demo keys
  (iss: supabase-demo, identical on every install, not secrets). Next loads
  .env.local above .env, so pointing at local changes no existing file and deleting
  it reverts to remote.
- supabase/config.toml: Twilio credentials replaced with env(TWILIO_*)
  interpolation and the skip-worktree flag cleared. The plaintext auth_token was
  tracked in git and was the reason merges kept aborting on this file. Rotation of
  the previously exposed token is still owed.
- packages/db/src/rls.db.test.ts: asserts the real grant surface — provider can
  update full_name/phone but not rating_avg, acceptance_rate, is_blocked or
  stripe_account_id; cannot touch role/kyc_status; cannot write service_skus; reads
  only its own service areas. Self-skips when 127.0.0.1:54321 is unreachable, so
  the suite still passes without Docker.

The escalation cases are one assertion per column, not a single four-column update.
Postgres rejects an UPDATE if any named column lacks privilege, so a combined
statement stays blocked while three of four are still revoked — it only goes red
once all four regress, hiding the realistic case of one column added back.

Each attempted value is also derived from the current value so it is always
different. A fixed payload made the test unfalsifiable: the first run under a
regressed grant writes that value for real, and every later run writes the same
number, so before === after and it passes forever with the hole wide open.

Verified: local grants match production exactly (avatar_url, bio, full_name,
notification_prefs, phone; anon none). 48 migrations replay clean on an empty DB.
60 tests pass. Granting only rating_avg fails exactly one test and no others;
revoking restores green. Production left untouched — 48 migrations, unchanged
grants, zero corrupted rows.
